pull_request.title: Share explicit fixture runtime bootstrap
pull_request.body:
IC Storage's collection tests and benchmark repeat the authority/pool/declaration/runtime setup also used by FixtureCell. Add testing::fixture_runtime behind test-support with explicit backing, owner, namespace, stable-key list and geometry. It returns the admitted runtime without initializing collections.

FixtureCell reuses this setup while retaining its existing public error variants. New FixtureRuntimeError preserves typed declaration, grant, construction and bootstrap failures; failures retain ordinary ledger behavior and never trigger resets or backing replacement.

Validation: Updated against released IC Memory 0.46.0, preserving exclusive leases, narrowed exports and fixture ledger exports. All ten focused fixture tests pass, including multiple distinct allocations, rejected uncommitted opens, retained bytes, duplicate declarations, grant mismatch and geometry refusal. Focused tests pass on Rust 1.91; test-support Clippy and warning-free Rustdoc pass. IC Storage's three adapter integration tests and benchmark Wasm check pass in an isolated consumer using this contribution via a temporary Cargo patch. Full release validation was not run.

The consumer remains on published IC Memory until this helper is released. Its adoption patch is prepared and qualified separately; no production Git/path dependency is introduced.

issue.title: Share bounded sparse memory image fixture loading

repository.name: ic-memory
repository.description: Durable stable-memory allocation governance for Internet Computer canisters

issue.body:
Jobs currently expands sparse frozen memory images locally before checking that retired ledgers are refused without writes. Add `testing::memory_from_sparse_hex(pages, runs, maximum_pages)` so Memory owns the fixture backing mechanics. Jobs keeps image provenance, its JSON schema, payload admission and both fresh/recovery refusal assertions.

The helper creates fresh zero-filled VectorMemory only, under an explicit page ceiling. It validates address bounds and ASCII hexadecimal runs before backing allocation, preserves gaps/trailing zeros and applies overlaps in input order. `SparseMemoryImageError` carries typed page/run/growth refusals. It never opens a runtime, recovers allocation authority, converts formats or accepts existing backing. The API is behind `test-support`; dependencies, package versions and runtime/storage contracts are unchanged. Compatible pending notes are 0.46.1 against released 0.46.0; the owner's pending 0.47 work remains separate.

Validation on Linux x86_64:
- Five focused producer tests pass on actual Rust 1.91: exact bytes/gaps/page boundaries/overlaps, page ceilings, malformed/non-ASCII hex, out-of-bounds runs, empty images and substrate growth refusal.
- Strict library/test Clippy, Rust 1.91 Wasm with test-support, warning-denied Rust 1.91 rustdoc, formatting and changed-document link checks pass. The link check used Jobs' reviewed Shared 0.16 checker; no tooling payload was copied into Memory.
- An isolated Jobs caller passes 25 consumer tests, 19 composition tests and one independent comparison reproducing both complete frozen backings byte for byte with the previous expansion. The caller's Wasm floor and strict Clippy also pass. All package names/versions remain selected; only Memory's source/checksum lock row is substituted for qualification.

Jobs' active registry dependency and local expansion remain until reviewed publication; the adoption patch is prepared separately. This contribution is independent of #120's fixture-runtime bootstrap. No full release suite, native macOS, live PocketIC, reset, release or publication ran. No sibling checkout was modified.

+//! Fixture-only runtime bootstrap shared by cells and collection qualification.
+use crate::{
+    GenericAllocationPolicy, Memory, MemoryAllocationPool, MemoryAuthority, MemoryManagerConfig,
+    MemoryRequest, MemoryRuntime, SealedDeclarationSnapshot,
+};
+
+/// Failure to construct and admit an explicitly configured fixture runtime.
+#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
+#[non_exhaustive]
+pub enum FixtureRuntimeError {
+    /// Invalid owner, stable key or declaration snapshot.
+    #[error(transparent)]
+    Declaration(#[from] crate::MemoryDeclarationError),
+    /// Invalid namespace grant or allocation pool.
+    #[error(transparent)]
+    AllocationPool(#[from] crate::MemoryAllocationPoolError),
+    /// Backing layout or configured geometry was refused.
+    #[error(transparent)]
+    Construction(#[from] crate::RuntimeConstructionError),
+    /// Runtime bootstrap or protected ledger recovery failed.
+    #[error(transparent)]
+    Bootstrap(Box<crate::RuntimeBootstrapError<std::convert::Infallible>>),
+}
+
+/// Bootstrap explicitly named fixture allocations using the ordinary runtime.
+///
+/// The caller supplies backing memory, one owner/namespace, stable keys and bucket
+/// geometry. No Cell or collection is initialized. Returns the runtime so callers
+/// can open multiple committed allocations or exercise rejected opens. Retained
+/// backing is admitted by normal bootstrap; errors never trigger a reset/fallback.
+/// This fixture helper uses the generic allocation policy and no exclusions;
+/// production policy/composition callers must configure their own runtime.
+///
+/// # Errors
+/// Preserves typed declaration, pool, construction and bootstrap failures.
+/// Bootstrap retains its ordinary ledger publication and recovery behavior.
+/// # Panics
+/// Backing memory IO retains its substrate panic behavior.
+pub fn fixture_runtime<M: Memory>(
+    backing: M,
+    owner: &str,
+    namespace: &str,
+    stable_keys: &[&str],
+    config: MemoryManagerConfig,
+) -> Result<MemoryRuntime<M>, FixtureRuntimeError> {
+    let requests = stable_keys
+        .iter()
+        .map(|key| MemoryRequest::new(owner, key))
+        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+    let pool = MemoryAllocationPool::new(vec![MemoryAuthority::new(owner, namespace)?], vec![])?;
+    let declarations = SealedDeclarationSnapshot::new(requests)?;
+    let mut runtime = MemoryRuntime::new_with_config(backing, config)?;
+    runtime
+        .bootstrap(&declarations, &pool, &GenericAllocationPolicy)
+        .map_err(|error| FixtureRuntimeError::Bootstrap(Box::new(error)))?;
+    Ok(runtime)
+}
+
+// Preserve the existing cell API and its error variants while sharing setup.
+impl From<FixtureRuntimeError> for super::FixtureCellError {
+    fn from(error: FixtureRuntimeError) -> Self {
+        match error {
+            FixtureRuntimeError::Declaration(error) => Self::Declaration(error),
+            FixtureRuntimeError::AllocationPool(error) => Self::AllocationPool(error),
+            FixtureRuntimeError::Construction(error) => Self::Construction(error),
+            FixtureRuntimeError::Bootstrap(error) => Self::Bootstrap(error),
+        }
+    }
+}
